name: mirage
text: CLV audit, first pass, from the engine's own saved lines (no new API calls): research/clv_audit_2026-10-21.md. What it shows: (1) only 164 of 612 listed bets have any CLV at all (27%), so the CLV picture is thin. (2) The close sources differ a lot: Novig's own 'last trades' close (often 3-10 trades) is the noisiest and the worst-looking (-0.6%); the sharp closes read better: Pinnacle via SGO +0.8% (47 bets), Circa +3.2% (11), DraftKings via ESPN +2.6% (20). (3) Your 373 listed settled bets are at +0.7% ROI against a claimed edge of +3.4%, but the standard error is 5.5%, so that cannot separate 0% from +3%. So 'beating CLV but losing' is mostly small sample plus a mixed close. Not yet verified: whether the Pinnacle closes themselves are accurate; next I'll join the PropLine archive (Pinnacle and Novig closes) to the same bets to lift coverage and compare sources bet by bet.
